editorial:
Imagine moving across the world to start over, only to realize you have no clue how anything works. That is exactly what you get with Braulio, Rafa, and Hakan. After their mess of a time in Berlin, they land in Hong Kong thinking they can easily find success. The vibe is lighthearted and chaotic, focusing on the funny side of culture shock. You will see them struggle with the language barrier and get into some pretty wild situations because they just do not understand the local customs. It feels like a road trip movie, but instead of a car, they are navigating a massive, neon-lit city where they are completely out of their element.

What really works here is the chemistry between the three leads; they feel like real friends who just happen to be bad at planning. The pacing is quick, though some of the jokes might feel a bit repetitive if you are not in the mood for slapstick humor. If you want something easy to watch on a Friday night, this is it.
endingExplained: After plenty of mistakes and funny arguments, the group finally learns how to respect the local culture. They stop trying to force their own way of doing things and start listening to the people around them. By the end, they manage to find a bit of stability and success in their careers. The movie wraps up with them realizing that friendship is the only thing that truly helps you survive in a strange land.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves fish-out-of-water comedies and stories about friendship.
